A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DS framework, with matching medical datasets, method components and retained results. All 17 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their equations, figures, tables and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical fine-tuning results, component ablations, GPT-4 comparisons, threshold experiments and a domain-shift analysis.

after.justification: v2 reports original pilot experiments, medical evaluations and ablations, plus CaseHOLD and MMLU experiments in Section 5.

M1.justification: The target-model quality filtering, three perplexity-based difficulty measures, attention weighting, intermediate difficulty selection and K-Center sampling remain intact. v2 selects the already-existing mean-attention variant as its principal configuration. Added K-Center pseudocode and embedding details explain the existing procedure rather than introduce a new component.

E1.justification: v2 retains the Chinese medical training collection and CMB-Exam, MMCU-Medical and CMB-Clin evaluations, while adding English legal reasoning on CaseHOLD and general-domain evaluation across MMLU's 57 subjects. This substantially expands domain, language and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Alpagasus and DEITA to the medical benchmark and pairwise comparisons. Its pilot study compares DeepSeek-R1 scoring with target-model scoring, and Appendix G.2 adds evaluated medical-model comparators Meditron-7B, HuatuoGPT-II-7B and HuatuoGPT-II-34B. The original main comparison methods remain represented.

E3.justification: v2 removes Baichuan2-7B and adds Qwen2.5-7B and LLaMA3-8B configurations. New protocols include external-versus-self-scoring controls, stage and budget experiments, and CaseHOLD evaluation using 5K selected training samples and 1K test samples. Pairwise judging is reported as GPT-4o instead of GPT-4, without establishing that retained comparisons were rerun. The original basic medical fine-tuning budget and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds stage-removal and stage-collapse ablations, difficulty-metric correlation and overlap analyses, 3K–7K budget sensitivity, and K-Center versus full-pool evaluation. Existing component ablations and two threshold curves are retained or relocated. v1's 500-sample domain-shift analysis, max-attention comparison, only-D1 variant and Baichuan2-7B analyses are removed.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 explicitly reports that most main experiments use one run, supplies three-run random-selection variability in Appendix E, and reports three-seed means and standard deviations for CaseHOLD. This adds limited uncertainty reporting; it does not establish repeated-run validation of the main 3DS results.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive pilot, backbone, baseline, ablation and cross-domain result entries, including CaseHOLD accuracy of 76.13% and MMLU accuracy of 65.08%. Matched mean-attention results are retained: Baichuan2-13B's CMB-Exam/MMCU scores remain 47.37/51.08, and Qwen1.5-7B's remain 61.96/66.09. Baichuan2-7B results and several variant and domain-shift findings disappear.

T1.justification: The difficulty definitions and attention-weighted calculations retain their mathematical substance. v2's explicit fixed-budget optimization objective, K-Center pseudocode and standard evaluation formulas elaborate the existing task and procedures. No substantive new theoretical assumptions, results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central 3DS contribution remains, but v2 broadens its claimed demonstrated applicability from Chinese medicine to English law and general-domain tasks. The abstract's superiority claim changes from 'over 5.29%' to 'up to 2.97%' under a revised comparison set. v1's claim of successful real-world medical deployment is omitted.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of stage-ablation effects, coarse verbal difficulty scores and complementary difficulty signals. It removes v1's domain-shift and reduced-overconfidence interpretation. New substantive limitations address selection occurring only before training, potentially valuable discarded samples, bias amplification through self-assessment, and population-specific limitations of Chinese medical data.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents LoRA rank, sequence cutoff, scheduler, warmup, precision, hardware, software versions, embedding extraction and the 280-example threshold-validation set. Appendices substantially expand baseline instructions, prompts and dataset provenance and maintenance information. The anonymous release pointer is replaced by stated public code and dataset access information; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands literature coverage to V-usable information, active learning, human problem-solving and confidence, additional medical models and datasets, cross-domain benchmarks, and fairness and safety. Section 6 explicitly distinguishes LLM data selection from active learning while retaining the central model-centric positioning. Earlier citations including D-CPT Law and Gemini Goes to Med School are omitted.

P1.justification: The introduction and motivation are extensively rewritten around a hypothesis, research questions and pilot findings. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, threshold analysis becomes Section 4.4, and algorithm and dataset material move into expanded appendices. The dataset description becomes a structured datasheet, alongside title, terminology and author-information edits.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1, restructures the main result tables with different backbone columns and averages, and separates ablations into dedicated tables. Dataset statistics and expanded pairwise plots move to appendices. New analytical tables, dataset examples and Algorithm 2 are added, while v1's domain-shift figure is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of previously unisolated design choices through stage/collapse and K-Center ablations, and addresses v1's medical-only validation with CaseHOLD and MMLU experiments. Expanded implementation and dataset documentation materially improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removal of some earlier analyses, although most main experiments are single-run and reporting errors remain, including Table 15's Baichuan2-13B comparison against removal of Stage 2, whose win/tie/loss percentages total 110%.
